answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring stake bonded to a verifiable work history: each new agent must lock collateral and complete a small, paid, time-locked task before its reputation counts, like an orchard where every tree must survive one tundra winter before bearing fruit. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus the time to grow each one, so an attacker standing on the ledge of profit finds the climb costs more than the harvest.
